recognize_zh: 兩顆帶狀/少分葉嗜中性球的細胞質中，靠近細胞膜邊緣處有小片淡藍灰色、邊界模糊的包涵體（Döhle body，殘留粗面內質網），同時伴隨明顯的毒性顆粒（toxic granulation），提示感染或發炎。
features: Two neutrophils (band/hyposegmented forms) with small, pale gray-blue, ill-defined peripheral cytoplasmic inclusions (Döhle bodies)
Prominent coarse azurophilic toxic granulation throughout the cytoplasm
Nuclei band-shaped to bilobed with condensed chromatin
Background normocytic red cells with an occasional echinocyte
Platelets normal in size and appearance
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows two neutrophils, band to hyposegmented in form, with coarse toxic granulation and small pale blue-gray, poorly circumscribed inclusions at the periphery of the cytoplasm, consistent with Döhle bodies. Red cells are largely unremarkable apart from an occasional echinocyte, and platelets are normal in size. Findings are consistent with reactive (toxic) neutrophil changes, typically seen in infection, inflammation, burns, pregnancy or G-CSF therapy.

ddx.vs: May-Hegglin inclusions are larger, sharper, spindle-shaped, occur in most neutrophils without toxic granulation, and are accompanied by giant platelets and thrombocytopenia.
Morulae are dense, stippled, purple-blue berry-like clusters of organisms, not pale homogeneous blue patches.
Chédiak-Higashi shows giant discrete red-purple granules rather than pale blue ribosomal inclusions.
Alder-Reilly shows dark coarse granules in all leukocytes without Döhle bodies and without clinical infection.
